content: Adalimumab is a medication that can increase your susceptibility to infections or worsen existing infections. Avoid close contact with individuals who have contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Inform your healthcare provider that you are using adalimumab before receiving any immunizations or vaccinations. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if absolutely necessary, as it may pose risks to an unborn baby. Discuss the potential risks and benefits with your doctor. Adalimumab can also pass into breast milk, so consult your healthcare provider if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Maintain a comprehensive list of all products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While using this medication, regular laboratory and medical tests, such as complete blood counts and liver function tests, should be conducted to monitor your condition and detect any potential side effects. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. Store adalimumab in the refrigerator and do not freeze it. Keep the medication in its original container to protect it from light. Some brands may also be stored at room temperature if necessary; consult your pharmacist or the product packaging for specific storage instructions. Discard any unused portion of the medication. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Adalimumab may rarely cause serious, potentially fatal liver disease in individuals exposed to the hepatitis B virus. Your doctor may order blood tests and monitor for symptoms during treatment and for several months after your last dose. A severe allergic reaction to this medication is rare. However, if you experience symptoms such as rash, itching, swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or difficulty breathing, seek immediate medical attention. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Common side effects may include redness, itching, pain, or swelling at the injection site. To minimize bruising, avoid rubbing the injection site after administration. Before using adalimumab, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, any of its components, or other adalimumab products. This medication may contain inactive ingredients, such as natural rubber or latex, which can cause allergic reactions or other issues. To use this medication, follow the instructions provided by your pharmacist and healthcare provider. Inject the medication under the skin as directed, typically every other week or once a week, depending on your condition. The injection is usually administered in the thigh or abdomen. Dosage is based on your medical condition, response to treatment, and, for children, weight. If you are treating conditions such as psoriasis, hidradenitis suppurativa, Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, or uveitis, your doctor may prescribe a different initial dosing schedule or higher dose. Before injecting, allow the medication to reach room temperature by removing it from the refrigerator 15 to 30 minutes prior. Do not warm the medication using other methods, such as microwaving or placing it in hot water. Inspect the product for particles or discoloration before use; do not use the liquid if either is present. Clean the injection site with rubbing alcohol before each dose and rotate injection sites to reduce the risk of skin injury. Avoid injecting into areas of skin that are sore, bruised, red, or hard. Use this medication consistently to achieve the best results. Mark your calendar to help you remember your dosing schedule. If you experience any side effects or have concerns, contact your doctor for medical advice.
